title: Weeknight Chicken Adobo
content: Filipino braise of chicken thighs in soy sauce, cane vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, and black peppercorns. One pot, ~45 minutes, mostly hands-off simmering. Salty-sour-savory; serve over white rice. Keeps beautifully - better the next day.

title: 15-Minute Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
content: Spaghetti tossed with shrimp seared in garlic butter, chili flakes, lemon juice, and parsley. Ready in 15 minutes flat - the fastest dinner in this collection. Weeknight-friendly with pantry staples plus a bag of frozen shrimp.

title: Sheet-Pan Miso-Glazed Salmon
content: Salmon fillets brushed with miso-maple glaze, roasted on one sheet pan with broccoli and sweet potatoes. 30 minutes, one pan to wash. Sweet-savory glaze caramelizes at the edges; great with rice or on its own for a low-carb dinner.

title: Classic French Omelette
content: Three eggs, butter, chives, and a nonstick pan. Two minutes of cooking but real technique: constant stirring, no color, rolled seam-side down. The dish cooks learn to prove they can cook. Serve with dressed greens.

title: Slow-Cooker Texas Chili
content: Beef chuck, dried ancho and chipotle chiles, no beans - Texas rules. Eight hours in the slow cooker, deeply smoky and rich. Make a day ahead for best flavor. Feeds eight; freezes for months. Top with sharp cheddar and raw onion.

title: Mushroom Risotto
content: Arborio rice cooked slowly with white wine, stock, parmesan, and a mix of cremini and dried porcini. About 40 minutes of stirring - a meditative weekend dish, not a rush job. Creamy without any cream. Vegetarian if made with vegetable stock.

title: Chana Masala
content: Chickpeas simmered in a spiced tomato-onion gravy with garam masala, cumin, and amchur for tang. 35 minutes with canned chickpeas, entirely from pantry staples. Vegan, hearty, and cheap - the ultimate meatless weeknight dinner with rice or naan.

title: Beef Bourguignon
content: The weekend project: beef braised three hours in red wine with pearl onions, mushrooms, and lardons. Julia Child's classic, worth every minute. Needs a full bottle of burgundy and an afternoon. Serve with crusty bread or mashed potatoes for a dinner party centerpiece.

title: Crispy Tofu Stir-Fry with Peanut Sauce
content: Cornstarch-dusted tofu pan-fried until shattering-crisp, tossed with snap peas and peppers in a peanut-lime sauce. 25 minutes, vegan, and the tofu method converts skeptics. Sauce doubles as a salad dressing.

title: Shakshuka
content: Eggs poached directly in a spiced tomato-pepper sauce with cumin and smoked paprika, finished with feta and cilantro. One skillet, 30 minutes, works for breakfast, brunch, or dinner. Mop up the sauce with warm pita.

title: Pork Carnitas Tacos
content: Pork shoulder braised with orange, lime, and oregano until it shreds, then crisped under the broiler. Three hours mostly unattended; feeds a crowd of six to eight. Serve in corn tortillas with white onion, cilantro, and salsa verde - taco night's main event.

title: Caprese Farro Salad
content: Chewy farro with cherry tomatoes, mozzarella pearls, basil, and balsamic. 30 minutes, served room temperature, and it holds all day - the ideal potluck or meal-prep lunch. Add white beans to make it a full vegetarian dinner.

title: Miso Ramen with Soft Egg
content: Weeknight ramen: miso-chicken broth built in 30 minutes, fresh noodles, a jammy seven-minute egg, corn, and scallions. Not a 48-hour tonkotsu - and that's the point. Deeply comforting on a cold night.

title: Greek Sheet-Pan Chicken with Lemon Potatoes
content: Chicken thighs and potato wedges roasted with lemon, garlic, and oregano; finished with olives and feta. 50 minutes, one pan. The potatoes soak up the lemony pan juices - arguably the best part.

title: Vegan Lentil Bolognese
content: Brown lentils and finely diced mushrooms simmered in tomato with red wine and a parmesan-free umami boost from soy sauce. 45 minutes; tastes like it cooked all day. Serve over rigatoni. Freezes well for meal prep.

title: Korean Beef Bulgogi Bowls
content: Thin-sliced ribeye marinated in soy, pear, garlic, and sesame, seared hot and served over rice with quick-pickled cucumbers. 30 minutes plus marinating. Sweet-savory and kid-approved; use the marinade on chicken too.

title: Butternut Squash Soup
content: Roasted butternut squash blended with onion, ginger, and coconut milk. 50 minutes, naturally vegan, and it freezes perfectly. Garnish with toasted pepitas and chili oil. The make-ahead starter for any fall dinner party.

title: Homemade Margherita Pizza
content: 24-hour cold-fermented dough, crushed San Marzano tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, basil. A weekend project: the dough needs a day, the bake needs your oven's maximum heat and a steel or stone. Makes two 12-inch pies - better than delivery, honestly.
